# FDG3032

> DO NOT use the same name for a namespace and a type in that namespace.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 3.4 Names of Namespaces.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1724
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library suggestion, application suggestion, test none
- Status: draft

CA1724 reports a type whose name matches a namespace, including namespaces of referenced assemblies that the type is not in, such as a type Data and System.Data (probe with SDK 10.0.402); the rule text covers only a type in that namespace, so those reports are not violations. Noise: lowered to suggestion (2 false positives of 3 reports). Renaming a public type changes the public API, so the fix is breaking; CA1724 has no code fix.

## From the book

For example, do not use `Debug` as a namespace name and then also provide a class named `Debug` in the same namespace. Several compilers require such types to be fully qualified.

These guidelines cover general namespace naming guidelines, but the next section provides specific guidelines for certain special subnamespaces.
